questions_used.question: All 23 relations, or the main paths?
questions_used.answer: All of them. Every relation once. I'd rather navigate a big canvas than lose a path.

questions_used.question: One canvas or several separate panes?
questions_used.answer: One canvas with everything, split into named diagrams I can read. Describe each one so I know what I'm looking at.

questions_used.question: Motion?
questions_used.answer: Slow, sparse dots — one per live transition. Nothing on the historical ones, and no dot sitting on a border.

questions_used.question: How many C4 levels, and what sits inside the manager box at each?
questions_used.answer: Four levels: L0 context (the manager as one box), L1 the manager's boundary services, L1b the machine side, L2 the inside. Membership follows the source: boundary services (private gRPC, webapi, registry, reconcile, SSH+BMC ops, boot server) at L1; the API surfaces plus queue at L1b; the whole internal service set at L2.
questions_used.reason: the owner's review names L0 and keeps the previous L1/L1b/L2; the source's own edge groups (request / heartbeat / ops) decide which services are boundary-facing

questions_used.question: Does L0 repeat the 23 relations at coarser endpoints?
questions_used.answer: No. L0 carries coarse context arrows (one per external actor, labelled with the why) plus the single external-to-external relation mch -> s3; the 23 atomic relations are drawn once each at their most-fitting level.
questions_used.reason: the task freezes 'all 23 relations once each at their most-fitting level'; duplicating them at L0 and L1 would break that, and dropping L0's arrows would leave the context picture unexplained

questions_used.question: Does every level need a container or a double border?
questions_used.answer: No. L0's manager is a single ordinary node — no container, no focus; L1/L1b/L2/L2b use containers; focus is used nowhere.
questions_used.reason: the owner's review says the double border is unnecessary and that L0's point is the surrounding world, not containment

questions_used.question: How much text at the top?
questions_used.answer: One to three wrapped rows per diagram (~250-290 characters) that name what is inside the box, what is outside, and how the diagram relates to its neighbours.
questions_used.reason: the frozen build wraps a description onto three 96-column rows; each description was measured so none clips

questions_used.question: Must the manager's whole inside share one diagram?
questions_used.answer: No — it splits into L2 (queue and dispatch) and L2b (the state writes) because the ten internal relations do not route as one diagram.
questions_used.reason: measured: three pinned orderings fail routing and the engine-ranked one draws 14 near-misses (records v1/v2/l2-c3/p4)

diagrams.title: L0 · System context
diagrams.description: System context: the machine manager is one box. The control plane and humans + mmctl call it; it drives the bare-metal providers, boots and audits the machines, which pull their boot image from S3, and it alerts in Slack. Nothing inside is shown yet, so L1 opens it.

diagrams.title: L1 · The machine manager
diagrams.description: L0's box opened one level: its boundary services — private gRPC, webapi, provider registry, cluster reconcile, SSH + BMC ops and the boot server — sit in the Machine manager box, while the control plane, humans, providers and machines stay outside it.
diagrams.capture_citation: evidence/canvas/canvas-whole-173x128-frames.txt rows 24-54 (divider, title, description rows 26-28, container rows 34-54)

diagrams.title: L1b · The machine side
diagrams.description: The fleet end of the same system. Bare-metal machines run the machine-agent, which registers and heartbeats into public gRPC inside the manager's box; the River queue uploads diagnostics to S3 and webapi confirms actions in Slack, both outside. The fleet drives these outward relations.
diagrams.capture_citation: evidence/canvas/canvas-whole-173x128-frames.txt rows 55-78 (divider, title, description rows 57-59, container around q/wapi/pub)

diagrams.title: L2 · Inside — queue and dispatch
diagrams.description: Inside the box, first slice: requests land on the River queue, which dispatches provision jobs to the provider registry, audit work to SSH + BMC ops and diagnostic events to the janitor; the janitor proposes actions back to webapi. L2b carries the state writes this slice leaves out.

diagrams.title: L2b · Inside — the state writes
diagrams.description: Inside the box, second slice: the writes into the Postgres state store — job rows from the queue, machine rows from private gRPC, machine state from public gRPC heartbeats and cluster state from the reconcile loop. Same box, same manager; only the state edges are drawn here.
